const r = await tools.exec_command({cmd:"cat > /tmp/donor-design-luna.md <<'EOF'
# Individual donor parsing design sketch

## Grounded shape

`FunderNameFeatures::from_name` is the single derivation point. It retains `name_raw`, builds normalized/token forms, and derives `person_core` by skipping leading words in a local title string allowlist. That list is repeated only here today. The feature struct serializes flat into `FunderObservation`; `funders_schema()` in `outbound/declaration_cleaning.rs` mirrors those serialized fields for `funders.parquet`. Existing parentheses evidence is separately captured by `parenthetical_text` and `has_unbalanced_parentheses`; `primary_name` has its own careful depth-aware handling for trading-as aliases.

## Caller shape

```rust
let name = FunderNameFeatures::from_name(Some("Lord (Alex) Ashcroft"));
// name.person_title == Some(PersonTitle::Lord)
// name.person_name_normalized == Some("alex ashcroft")
// name.person_display_normalized == Some("lord alex ashcroft")
```

For `Mr James Smith`, keep the raw spelling unchanged, store `Mr` as the title, and store `james smith` as the normalized person name. Do not infer given/surname fields. For organizations, withheld names, and names with no recognized leading title, the new person-specific fields are null; all existing generic and organization features retain their behavior.

## Candidate A — typed title plus normalized person-name candidate (recommended)

Add one canonical `PersonTitle` enum in `funder_name.rs` for the existing leading honorific vocabulary (including `mr`, `mrs`, `ms`, `miss`, `mx`, `dr`, `prof`, `professor`, `sir`, `dame`, `lord`, `lady`, `rev`, `reverend`, `rt`, `hon`). Give it a single normalized-string mapping and serde representation. Parse only a contiguous recognized prefix of normalized tokens, preserving the current multi-title consumption behavior. `person_core` can continue to be derived from the remainder, now through this enum parser, avoiding a second vocabulary.

Add nullable `person_title: Option<PersonTitle>` and `person_name_normalized: Option<String>` fields to `FunderNameFeatures`. The name field is the normalized remainder after recognized leading title tokens and punctuation normalization; it is not a first/last split. For usual names this derives from existing `name_tokens`. For the explicit pattern `lord (Name) Surname`, allow the parenthetical text to fill the person-name remainder only when the whole leading normalized pattern is `lord`, a balanced single parenthetical group, and trailing nonempty tokens. The source remains untouched and `parenthetical_text` continues recording the exact contents. This narrow exception avoids interpreting arbitrary organization parentheses as a person name.

Add matching nullable UTF-8 columns `person_title` and `person_name_normalized` beside `person_core` in `funders_schema()`. Serde's enum string form should agree with the schema's snake-case values. This is additive to cleaned Parquet rows and doesn't alter funder matching or database identity.

## Candidate B — tagged person-name value

Instead of two optional fields on `FunderNameFeatures`, add `person: Option<ParsedPersonName>` where `ParsedPersonName { title: Option<PersonTitle>, name_normalized: String }`. It makes the title/name relationship explicit and avoids combinations such as title without a name. Serialization could flatten the nested fields for Parquet, but then the implementation needs deliberate serde/schema alignment (or a custom serialize projection); leaving it nested creates a Parquet struct and expands downstream schema changes. This is structurally stronger but adds interface and schema machinery for a currently flat feature record.

## Comparison / decision

Choose Candidate A for the smallest additive interface: it fits the existing flat parallel-feature contract and existing explicit Parquet schema. Ensure both values are emitted together only when a nonempty post-title person-name candidate exists; use `None` for both otherwise. Keep `person_core`'s established title-stripped behavior. The enum is the sole source of title vocabulary, and no surname/given-name assumptions are introduced.

Candidate B is preferable only if callers need to pass the two values around as one semantic unit or enforce their co-presence outside this serializer. Current evidence shows one flattened serialized feature row and no such caller, so the pair plus a construction invariant at the one derivation point is the narrower fit.

## Ownership and boundaries

- `FunderNameFeatures::from_name`: owns parsing and invariants; external text becomes normalized typed title/name evidence here.
- `PersonTitle`: owns the finite supported title vocabulary and normalized serialized spelling.
- `FunderObservation`: remains a transparent flattened consumer; no entity classification or identity decision is added.
- `funders_schema()`: adds the two nullable columns in the same order as serialization.
- Existing raw name, organization fields, aliases, acronym evidence, and parenthetical evidence remain independently available and unchanged.

## Behavior checks for implementation

- `Mr James Smith` => title `mr`, normalized name `james smith`.
- `Mrs Jane Doe`, `Dame Jane Doe`, and `Lord Alex Ashcroft` => expected distinct titles and remainder.
- `Lord (Alex) Ashcroft` => title `lord`, normalized name `alex ashcroft`; exact raw and parenthetical evidence preserved.
- `Example (Alex) Ltd`, unbalanced parentheses, withheld/missing names, and names without a recognized prefix => new fields null; existing organization/name outputs unchanged.
- Two or more recognized leading titles are all removed from `person_core`; select a deterministic title policy (prefer the first recognized token) and document it in tests.
- Verify JSON serialization and a cleaned `funders.parquet` round trip/schema include both columns.
EOF","workdir":"/Users/jamie/development/exposed.improve-individual-donor-parsing","max_output_tokens":200});
